messages:
kevin: Quick question — we're designing the canary traffic split UX and policy. Need a plan so partner header overrides (X-Partner-Canary) don't accidentally bypass telemetry sampling or sticky routing.
aj: Agree. Two constraints: 1) headers should be honored for explicit partner-driven tests 2) we still need consistent metrics and sampling for internal A/B.
tess: Can we treat header overrides as a higher-priority hint but require an opt-in flag on the partner account? Otherwise partners could route >100% traffic to canary.
maria: +1. Also: what about sticky session behavior? If a user gets assigned canary via weight, they should stick for a window so telemetry maps to a user cohort.
kevin: Proposed policy: order of evaluation -> explicit route match (path/host) -> header override (only for whitelisted partners) -> weighted split -> fallback. Sticky cookie/session id used to maintain assignment for 24h.
sam-ci: For telemetry: we need deterministic assignment so that p50/p95 comparisons between canary and stable are valid. Use hash(user_id || route_id) % 100 < weight. If header override present, apply only if partner_whitelisted flag true.
aj: Sounds good. How do we prevent partners from skewing latency metrics by sending huge synthetic loads? Need rate-limits + labeling.
tess: Label every request with routing_reason: one of [explicit_match, header_override, weighted_split, fallback]. That way analytics can filter. Also add partner_tag when applicable.
kevin: Example routing policy (pseudo):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "match": {"host": "api.redwood.ai", "method": "POST"},
  "canary": {
    "model": "redwood-model-x-canary",
    "weight": 10,
    "sticky_ttl_seconds": 86400,
    "header_override": {
      "header": "X-Partner-Canary",
      "whitelist": ["partner-a", "partner-b"]
    }
  },
  "fallback": "redwood-model-x-stable"
}
```
maria: One more: sampling of full payloads (for quality eval) must be opt-in per customer + scrubby by default. We can't store PII. So sample IDs only, plus hashed context.
sam-ci: For observability pipeline, add routing_reason as tag and a canary_id. Also emit assignment_decision log (why this request went to canary/stable). Keep those logs at debug level and scrubbed for prod.
aj: UX note for Console: show a small banner in canary view: current weight, active whitelisted header partners, sticky TTL, recent error delta (canary vs stable). Allow immediate rollback and a "force-metric-check" button (runs kakfa query + sanity checks).
tess: Edge-cases: if canary model errors out, we should fallback on the same request and emit a metric for fallback_rate. Also if header_override points to an invalid canary, ignore and log.
kevin: Anyone oppose using integer weight (0-100) or do we want per-route decimals? Integer is simpler; hashing gives distribution. Can revisit later.
maria: Integer OK. Add a guard: if traffic < 1% but request volume is too low, flag insufficient sample in the console.
aj: Implementation notes: runtime needs to expose hooks: assign_canary(user_id, route_id, weight) -> {assignment, reason, canary_id}. Make it pluggable for Dedicated/Private.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary-routing-v2 -> staging at 1748001285 :rocket:
kevin: Cool. Next steps: write RFC with policy, add example policy JSON, and add console mockups for toggles and reason filters. I'll open the RFC in docs and cc @maria @aj.
maria: I'll draft the telemetry tags + privacy checklist.
tess: I'll mock a minimal console panel and submit a PR for the frontend toggle. :thumbsup:
aj: I'll pick up runtime integration and the whitelist config in the SRE store.
kevin: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open for two days for comments. :eyes:
